items.title: Section: Hearing Closes, and Reflecting on the True Teaching Opens

items.zh: 云何思正法？謂如有一，即如所聞、所信正法，獨處空閑，遠離六種不應思處。謂思議我、思議有情、思議世間、思議有情業果異熟、思議靜慮者靜慮境界、思議諸佛諸佛境界。但正思惟所有諸法自相、共相。
items.en: What is reflecting on the true teaching? It means that one, dwelling alone in solitude, reflects on the true teaching just as it was heard and believed, while avoiding six things that should not be speculated upon: speculating about the self, about sentient beings, about the world, about the actions of sentient beings, about the ripening of their results, about the meditative states of accomplished meditators, and about the states of the Buddhas. Instead, one correctly reflects only on the specific and general characteristics of all phenomena.

items.title: Two Methods of Reflection: Numerical Enumeration and the Five Aggregates

items.zh: 如是思惟，復有二種。一者、以算數行相，善巧方便算計諸法；二者、以稱量行相，依正道理觀察諸法功德過失。謂若思惟諸蘊相應所有言教，若復思惟如前所說所餘隨一所有言教，皆由如是二種行相方便思惟。此復云何？謂言色者，即十色處，及墮法處所攝眾色，是名色蘊。所言受者，即三種受，是名受蘊。所言想者，即六想身，是名想蘊。所言行者，即六思身等，是名行蘊。所言識者，即六識身等，是名識蘊。
items.en: Such reflection is, moreover, of two kinds: first, reflection through the mode of enumeration, skilfully calculating phenomena by number; second, reflection through the mode of evaluation, examining the merits and faults of phenomena according to correct reasoning. … As for form: it is the ten form-fields, together with the various forms comprised within the mental field — this is called the aggregate of form. As for feeling: it is the three kinds of feeling — this is called the aggregate of feeling. As for perception: it is the six groups of perception — this is called the aggregate of perception. As for formations: it is the six groups of volition, and so on — this is called the aggregate of formations. As for consciousness: it is the six groups of consciousness, and so on — this is called the aggregate of consciousness.

items.zh: 如是名為以算數行相，思惟諸蘊相應言教。或復由此算數行相，別別思惟展轉差別，當知即有無量差別。

items.title: Section: Evaluative Reflection Opens — The Principle of Dependence

items.zh: 云何以稱量行相，依正道理思惟諸蘊相應言教？謂依四道理無倒觀察。何等為四？一、觀待道理，二、作用道理，三、證成道理，四、法爾道理。云何名為觀待道理？謂略說有二種觀待。一、生起觀待，二、施設觀待。生起觀待者，謂由諸因、諸緣勢力生起諸蘊，此蘊生起要當觀待諸因、諸緣。施設觀待者，謂由名身、句身、文身施設諸蘊，此蘊施設要當觀待名句文身。是名於蘊生起觀待、施設觀待。
items.en: What is it to reflect through the mode of evaluation, examining teaching connected with the aggregates according to correct reasoning? It means observing without distortion according to four principles. What are the four? The principle of dependence, the principle of function, the principle of proof, and the principle of natural law. What is the principle of dependence? Briefly, there are two kinds of dependence: dependence in arising, and dependence in designation. Dependence in arising means that the aggregates arise through the power of various causes and conditions — their arising necessarily depends on those causes and conditions. Dependence in designation means that the aggregates are designated through bodies of names, phrases, and letters — their designation necessarily depends on those names, phrases, and letters. This is called dependence in the arising and designation of the aggregates.

items.zh: 即此生起觀待、施設觀待，生起諸蘊、施設諸蘊，說名道理瑜伽方便，是故說為觀待道理。

items.title: The Principle of Function: Each Phenomenon Does Its Own Distinct Work

items.zh: 云何名為作用道理？謂諸蘊生已，由自緣故，有自作用，各各差別。謂眼能見色，耳能聞聲，鼻能嗅香，舌能甞味，身能覺觸，意能了法。色為眼境，為眼所行；乃至法為意境，為意所行。或復所餘如是等類，於彼彼法別別作用，當知亦爾。
items.en: What is meant by the principle of function? It means that, once the aggregates have arisen, each has its own distinct function, arising from its own specific conditions, each function differing from the others. The eye is able to see form; the ear is able to hear sound; the nose is able to smell odour; the tongue is able to taste flavour; the body is able to feel touch; the mind is able to cognize phenomena. Form is the eye's object, the eye's domain of activity; and so on, up through phenomena being the mind's object, the mind's domain of activity. And for all other such categories of phenomena, each has its own distinct function in just the same way.

items.zh: 即此諸法各別作用所有道理瑜伽方便，皆說名為作用道理。

items.title: Section: The Principle of Proof — Three Ways of Knowing Something Is True

items.zh: 云何名為證成道理？謂一切蘊皆是無常，眾緣所生，苦、空、無我。由三量故，如實觀察。謂由至教量故，由現量故，由比量故。由此三量證驗道理。諸有智者，心正執受、安置、成立。謂一切蘊皆無常性、眾緣生性、苦性、空性，及無我性。如是等名證成道理。
items.en: What is meant by the principle of proof? It means that all the aggregates are impermanent, arisen from various conditions, suffering, empty, and without self — and this is observed truly by means of three measures: authoritative scripture, direct perception, and inference. By these three measures, the principle is verified. Those who are wise correctly grasp, establish, and confirm it in their minds — namely, that all the aggregates have the nature of impermanence, the nature of being dependently arisen, the nature of suffering, the nature of emptiness, and the nature of non-self. This is called the principle of proof.

items.title: The Principle of Natural Law: Facts That Simply Are What They Are

items.zh: 云何名為法爾道理？謂何因緣故，即彼諸蘊如是種類，諸器世間如是安布？何因緣故，地堅為相、水濕為相、火煖為相、風用輕動以為其相？何因緣故，諸蘊無常、諸法無我、涅槃寂靜？
items.en: What is meant by the principle of natural law? It concerns questions such as: for what reason are the aggregates of just these kinds, and the physical world arranged just this way? For what reason does earth have solidity as its characteristic, water moisture, fire heat, and wind light movement? For what reason are the aggregates impermanent, all phenomena without self, and nirvana peaceful?

items.title: Section: Natural Law Closes the Four Principles, and Hearing-and-Reflecting Completes

items.zh: 何因緣故，色變壞相、受領納相、想等了相、行造作相、識了別相？由彼諸法本性應爾、自性應爾、法性應爾，即此法爾，說名道理瑜伽方便。或即如是、或異如是、或非如是，一切皆以法爾為依，一切皆歸法爾道理，令心安住、令心曉了。如是名為法爾道理。如是名為依四道理，觀察諸蘊相應言教。如由算數行相及稱量行相，觀察諸蘊相應言教，如是即由二種行相，觀察其餘所有言教。如是總名審正觀察思惟一切所說正法。如是名為聞思正法。
items.en: For what reason does form have the mark of change and decay, feeling the mark of experiencing, perception the mark of apprehending and cognizing, formations the mark of constructing, and consciousness the mark of discerning? Because these phenomena's basic nature, their own nature, their essential nature is simply so — this very "simply so" is called a mode of correct reasoning, called the principle of natural law. … Just as the modes of enumeration and evaluation are used to examine teaching connected with the aggregates, so too these same two modes are used to examine every other teaching. All of this, together, is called the careful and correct examination and reflection upon everything the true teaching sets forth. This is called hearing and reflecting on the true teaching.

blocks.text: How to reflect on what one has heard. The four principles of reasoning (四種道理) are one of the treatise's most important tools for thinking; they reappear in the *Saṃdhinirmocana Sūtra*.

In solitude, one reflects on the teaching as heard, avoiding six things: speculation about the self, beings, the world, beings' actions and their ripening, the meditator's domain, and the Buddhas' domain. Venerable Miào Jìng: Buddhism accepts a nominal self; "this 'I' is a name, not a reality".

**Enumeration**: counting phenomena (five aggregates, etc.). **Evaluation**: examining their merits and faults "according to correct reasoning". Master Cháng Bǎi: reasoning that accords with the three valid means of knowledge.

items: **Dependence** (觀待道理): the aggregates arise "through the power of various causes and conditions", and are named in relation to one another.
**Function** (作用道理): "each has its own distinct function": the eye sees form, the ear hears sound.

**Proof** (證成道理): that the aggregates are impermanent, suffering, empty, and non-self is established by **scripture**, **direct perception**, and **inference**. Venerable Miào Jìng: take all three together.

**Natural law** (法爾道理): why is earth solid, water wet? Why is form subject to change, feeling to experiencing? "Because these phenomena's nature is simply so." Master Cháng Bǎi: what is so from the start.

blocks.text: The four principles are a good test for any idea: What does it depend on? What does it do? How do we know it's true? And is it simply the way things are? The last principle is a recognition that explanation has limits.

quiz.q: Which six things should not be speculated upon, and how does Venerable Miào Jìng show that beings' karma is hard to fathom?
options: the self, beings, the world, beings' karma, its ripening, meditators' states, Buddhas' states; even an evildoer who attends wisely at death may not get a bad result
quiz.why: "Speculating about the self, about sentient beings, about the world, about the actions of sentient beings, about the ripening of their results, about the meditative states of accomplished meditators, and about the states of the Buddhas." Venerable Miào Jìng: one who did much evil but attends wisely at death may not get a bad result — there is change, so the doer's lot is not fixed.

quiz.q: Why should one not speculate about the self, and what kind of self does Venerable Miào Jìng say Buddhism accepts?
options: a nominal self — the "I" is a name, not something real
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: the scriptures speak of a nominal self; Buddhism accepts a nominal self — this "I" is a name, not a reality. Insisting it is real, or that there is nothing at all, falls into exaggeration or denial.

quiz.q: Which four principles guide evaluative reflection, and what does Master Cháng Bǎi say the principle of dependence does for practice?
options: dependence, function, proof, natural law; seeing that phenomena depend on conditions, one no longer grasps them as having fixed essence
quiz.why: "The principle of dependence, the principle of function, the principle of proof, and the principle of natural law." Master Cháng Bǎi: seeing that all phenomena exist in dependence on conditions, one no longer grasps them as having an unchanging essence.

quiz.q: How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain 待 in "dependence in arising"?
options: 待 means meeting — what conditions it meets determines whether it arises
quiz.why: "Dependence in arising means that the aggregates arise through the power of various causes and conditions." Venerable Miào Jìng: 待 is what it encounters — it depends on which conditions it meets before it can arise.

quiz.q: The principle of function says each aggregate has its function once arisen. When, according to Master Cháng Bǎi, does that function begin?
options: at the very moment of arising
quiz.why: "Once the aggregates have arisen, each has its own distinct function, arising from its own specific conditions." Master Cháng Bǎi: in the very moment of arising, as soon as it appears, it has its function.

quiz.q: The note, following the commentary, assigns "grasp, establish, confirm" to the three measures. What do the lectures say?
options: Miào Jìng prefers taking the three measures together as a process of cultivation; Cháng Bǎi: seeing by direct perception produces right view and plants roots of virtue — that is "establishing"
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: I think the three measures should be taken together — you take up all three, then cultivate yourself. Master Cháng Bǎi: observing through the four kinds of direct perception produces right view and plants roots of virtue for discipline, concentration, and wisdom — that is "establishing."

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi define "natural law" (法爾)?
options: simply so from the start — what cannot be further explained just is so
quiz.why: "Because these phenomena's basic nature, their own nature, their essential nature is simply so." Master Cháng Bǎi: what is so from the start is called 法爾 — what admits no further explanation simply is so.
